questions.q: What is soil erosion? Suggest measures for soil conservation.

answer.text: Soil erosion is the removal of the fertile topsoil by running water and wind. Running water may strip soil evenly as sheet erosion, or cut deep channels called gullies, which spread into badlands like the Chambal ravines. Wind blows away loose soil in dry regions. Deforestation, overgrazing and faulty methods of cultivation greatly speed up erosion.

On sloping land, ploughing along the contours, cutting terraces, and growing crops in alternate strips slow down the flow of water and check erosion. Belts of trees, called shelter belts, break the force of the wind in dry areas. Planting more trees, controlling grazing, rotating crops and building small check dams to plug gullies also protect the soil.

answer: Such measures preserve the fertile topsoil, on which agriculture and life depend.
